plotSections.title: The Helm and the Phylactery Question
bullets: The party debates whether the lich's phylactery could be split or fragmented, since they understood a phylactery to be a single item; Sylan notes Walker is the only one who looted the lich, and the keystone is ruled out as a candidate.
The DM recaps the conversation with Carlkin about a month earlier: the party strongly suspected the phylactery was something they had with them.

The Soul identifier (a small bag resembling a bag of holding) makes a true phylactery burst into flames immediately; the helm only smoldered because it holds a soul fragment or echo, a remembrance of a soul that is still strong enough to possess someone.
The helm is placed in the pouch again and confirmed not to be the phylactery; it is likened to a possessed doll from a B-rated horror film.
Walker refuses to dispose of the helm or give it to anyone else, reasoning that he has already resisted its possession and is the safest person to wear it.

The hunched eagle troop marker is tested in the Soul identifier with no smoldering or burning, so it is not the phylactery. Sylan and Ord have nothing suspicious to test; Ord suggests running every item the party owns through the bag.

plotSections.title: Evening at the Stronghold
bullets: Mahali discourages attempting possession before dinner and recommends it as a late-night endeavor; he serves summer cider, pork stew and assorted desserts, then goes to prep breakfast.
Gerk's punched potatoes ('Gerk tubers') were not part of dinner; Mahali plans to shred them into a breakfast hash, and Gerk begins to suspect he was used.

Walker agrees to try speaking with the helm's spirit again after dinner, in the dining hall where Mahali can watch; Sylan offers magical protection against possession, and Walker accepts a little help.
